title: Indexes, compound indexes and the order that makes them work

videos.script: A hundred thousand orders, and one customer wants to see hers. {{orders}} Without an index, MongoDB reads every one of the hundred thousand to find eighty-two. With one, it reads eighty-two. {{scan}} That much is what everybody expects. The interesting part is the index with two fields, because the order of the fields decides whether it helps. {{compound}} Put the status first and the date second, and the newest pending orders come out already sorted. Swap them, and the same two fields make the server walk thousands of entries it then throws away. {{order}} There is a rule for the order: equality, then sort, then range. You will watch it hold, and you will see the numbers when it is broken. {{esr}} Then two indexes that do more than find documents. One answers a query without opening a single document. The other indexes the inside of an array. {{covered}} And then the bill. Every index makes every write slower and takes memory. You will measure both. {{cost}} Last, three indexes that change behaviour rather than speed: one that refuses duplicates, one that covers only some documents, and one that deletes them. {{special}}
